Plan the validation of a bmm model

Source: R/validation-plan.R
validation_plan.Rd

Usage

validation_plan(
  model,
  pars = NULL,
  sds = NULL,
  cors = NULL,
  grid = NULL,
  reps = NULL,
  sampler = NULL,
  sbc = NULL,
  prior_check = NULL,
  reference = NULL,
  convergence = NULL,
  criteria = NULL,
  stages = NULL,
  formula = NULL,
  trial_design = NULL,
  generator = NULL,
  seed,
  owner = NULL,
  version = NULL
)

Arguments

model

A bmmodel, or the name of a model with a validation_defaults() entry, which is then built with the entry's variable names (bmm is needed for that).

pars

Named population values on the link scale, as in simulate_recovery().

sds

Named between-subject SDs on the link scale; NULL takes the entry's.

cors

A correlation matrix between subject values, as in simulate_recovery(); NULL takes the entry's, which may be none.

grid

A data frame with the columns n_subjects and n_trials, one row per design.

reps

Replications per design.

sampler

A named list passed to the fitter of every recovery cell (chains, iter, warmup, cores, backend, ...). A list given here changes the entries it names and keeps the others. It may not set prior or an abbreviation of it (pri), nor may sbc$sampler or prior_check$sampler: the calibration's prior is sbc$prior, and the recovery stage fits under bmm's default priors.

sbc

A named list for the calibration: n_subjects, n_trials, n_sims, prior (a brmsprior, a data frame with the columns of brms::set_prior(), or NULL for bmm's defaults), prior_reason (why it is not bmm's default, printed on the card), level, sampler, generator, cores_per_fit and thin_ranks (see sbc()). Named entries replace the entry's, the rest are kept, except that a prior other than the entry's, given without a prior_reason, drops the entry's reason. The prior is compared as given, column order and types included: a brmsprior with the same rows as an entry's data frame, the entry's columns in another order, or a factor column counts as another prior. A prior_reason without a prior is an error.

prior_check

A named list for the prior predictive check: n_subjects, n_trials, n_draws, range, range_reason (why the range is what it is, printed on the card), summary and sampler (see prior_check()). Merged as sbc is: a range other than the entry's, given without a range_reason, drops the entry's reason, and a range_reason without a range is an error. The range is compared as given, names included, so c(lo = 0.15, hi = 5) counts as another range than the entry's c(0.15, 5).

reference

NULL, or a reference implementation's estimates for the agreement stage: a data frame with term and estimate (and optionally ci_low, ci_high) on the natural scale, as cross_check() takes it, plus the provenance columns package, version, call, data_hash, date and source.

convergence

NULL for check_convergence()'s defaults, or a named list of its arguments, as in recovery_grid().

criteria

A named list replacing some of the default criteria (see "Criteria").

stages

NULL for every stage that exists, or the names of the stages to run (see "Stages"). The run record always runs; a stage that reads the recovery grid needs "recovery" too.

formula, trial_design, generator

As in recovery_grid(). NULL formula means recovery_formula() with correlated subject effects when there are at least two subject-varying parameters, so the individual-differences stage has correlations to score.

seed

The master seed, required. Each stage derives its own from it (see "Seeds").

owner, version

The entry's owner and plan version; NULL takes the entry's.

Value

A bmmtools_validation_plan: a named list with every field above resolved, plus model_name, defaults ("bmmtools <version> entry" or "none"), re_cor, correlations, seeds, stages (a tibble: stage, order, title, required, status, issue, reason), hash and bmmtools_version.

Details

Builds a bmmtools_validation_plan: everything run_validation() needs to validate one model, resolved before anything is fitted. Every argument left NULL is filled from the model's validation_defaults() entry, or for a model without one from the generic grid, in which case pars is required.

Stages

In card order: run_record, prior_predictive, sbc, recovery, computation, identifiability, individual_differences, data_requirements, agreement, model_recovery and posterior_checks. A stage is "planned"; "not built" with the issue that will build it (model recovery, #6; posterior checks, #20); "not applicable" with the reason (individual differences with fewer than two subject-varying parameters; data requirements without a subject-varying parameter, or without two numbers of trials at read_off_n_subjects subjects in the grid; agreement without a reference); or "excluded" when stages leaves it out. All but agreement, model recovery and posterior checks are required for a card to be called complete.

Criteria

prior_bound_rate_max (0.10): the largest floor or ceiling rate of the prior predictive draws under the calibration's prior; under bmm's defaults the rates are reported, not judged, unless the calibration uses them. sbc_ecdf_prob (0.95): the simultaneous band of SBC's ECDF-difference check no ranked variable may leave. convergence_rate_min (0.95): the share of recovery cells that pass check_convergence(). coverage_level (0.95) and coverage_alpha (0.05): the coverage of every population parameter, its intervals pooled over the designs, must not fall below coverage_level by a one-sided binomial test at coverage_alpha divided by the number of parameters; the generating correlations are held to the same test. contraction_min (0) and z_mean_max (2): the identifiability bars at the largest design. read_off_r_low (0.80) and read_off_n_subjects (50): the data requirements read-off, the smallest n_trials at which every subject-varying parameter's person-level r_low reaches the bar at that many subjects; 0.80 is a convention, and the read-off at 0.70 and 0.90 is reported beside it. tolerance: by metric, how far a number without a Monte Carlo standard error may move between two runs before compare_validations() flags it.

Seeds

The recovery grid runs under seed, the prior check under seed + 1 and the calibration under seed + 2. The seeds, the owner and the reasons (sbc$prior_reason, prior_check$range_reason) are left out of the plan's hash and of the stages' keys, so the hash changes only when what is planned changes, and rewording a reason reruns nothing.

See also

run_validation(), validation_defaults().

Examples

plan <- validation_plan(
  structure(
    list(links = list(kappa = "log", thetat = "logit")),
    class = c("bmmodel", "circular", "mixture2p")
  ),
  seed = 1
)
plan
#> <bmmtools validation plan> mixture2p, version 0.1.0, hash c6c12584
#> Owner: Gidon Frischkorn; defaults: bmmtools 0.3.0 entry
#> Truth (link scale): kappa = 2.08, thetat = 1.1
#> Subject SDs (link scale): kappa = 0.3, thetat = 0.5
#> Grid: 6 designs x 10 replications (n_subjects 20, 50; n_trials 30, 100, 300)
#> Sampler: chains = 4, iter = 2000, warmup = 1000, cores = 4, backend = "cmdstanr"
#> SBC: 100 simulations at 20 subjects x 50 trials under the plan's own prior
#> Prior check: 500 draws at 20 subjects x 50 trials
#> Reference: none
#> Seed: 1
#> Stages:
#>    1 run_record               planned        
#>    2 prior_predictive         planned        
#>    3 sbc                      planned        
#>    4 recovery                 planned        
#>    5 computation              planned        
#>    6 identifiability          planned        
#>    7 individual_differences   planned        
#>    8 data_requirements        planned        
#>    9 agreement                not applicable  no reference implementation
#>   10 model_recovery           not built       not run (#6)
#>   11 posterior_checks         not built       not run (#20)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
plan <- validation_plan("ezdm", seed = 20261024)
} # }
